findings.claim: The method proposal defines a non-search, publication-manifest-first route with deterministic planning constraints and explicitly prohibits network/source access during preparation.
findings.uncertainty: No concrete manifest execution has been run yet, so reproducibility remains at the design stage only.
findings.remediation: Keep this phase repository-only and require a separate owner authorization packet before any network activity.

findings.claim: Stop history shows 672 cumulative denied URLs in the last predecessor lineage and documents a terminal overlap failure where 615 observed URLs are designated exposure; the proposal correctly treats reuse as forbidden.
findings.uncertainty: This finding is bounded by local cumulative lineage artifacts and does not estimate true global universe overlap.
findings.remediation: Do not construct proposal execution frames that draw from previously denied candidates; treat exposure ledger extension as append-only evidence.

options.description: Use official publication manifests or public indexes as the single upstream source for candidate acquisition planning.
trade_offs: Lower semantic risk than broad crawling because only official disclosure surfaces are consumed.
Can be materially distinct from prior query-search rediscovery if manifest corpus is sufficiently authoritative and fixed.
limitations: Depends on host/index completeness and stable section semantics.
Manifest quality can block progress without additional legal or source-specific work.
options.contingency: Pause and return to this workstream with an expanded manifest governance plan if fixed manifests cannot be produced deterministically.

options.description: Use bounded directory traversals under fixed official host/domain trees as the second method.
trade_offs: Can discover candidate pages absent from formal manifests.
Maintains a second distinct route that avoids web search index dependence.
limitations: Higher parser/structure variance and higher parser-failure risk.
options.contingency: Only execute after full manifest failure and with updated stop rules and parent owner authorization.

recommendation: Proceed with Option A as the primary materially distinct route for design freeze, because it is the least rediscovery-prone and most directly aligned to non-search constraints. Build a fixed manifest universe in repository-only form first, then request a separate exact owner authorization before any execution.
rationale: Option A preserves the terminal exposure controls, minimizes adaptive reuse risk, and cleanly separates preparation from execution while keeping all prior cumulative-deny evidence intact.
conflicts: The proposal remains design-only and cannot reduce G2 blockers by itself without fresh owner authorization and execution lineage.
abstentions: No rights/privacy/security specialist review is performed here.
No source bytes were requested, opened, or extracted.
